Loud DJ music is permitted at full volume until 5 a.m., with no consideration for residents, senior citizens, children, or students—even during board exam periods. Alcohol consumption is openly allowed within the society premises and surrounding areas.

In addition to this, water shortage is a regular and serious issue in the society. This problem occurs every month throughout the year, and it becomes especially severe from March to July, making daily life extremely difficult for residents.

Due to frequent disturbances and poor basic facilities, the society is not suitable for families. Overall management is weak, and the living conditions do not justify even a ₹10,000 rent.

Please evaluate all these points carefully before making any decision.

The security here closes off the boundary gates of the footpath, so you're forced to walk through it all the way to exit. When you leave in the evening, as you walk through the footpath, you'd hear a common, periodic chant - "Tation! Tation! Tation!". The Auto wale uncles here are passionate and dedicated to one single task - to take you to the railway station, whether you like it or not. If you're a guy, they will pull you by your hand to take you to their autos, all while some try to grab you too to take you to THEIR autos. They don't even ask if you wish to go to the station or not. But looking at their passion, anyone will go with them even if their destination  isn't the station, such is the entrancing conviction they possess. To be honest, I love the attention. I mean, at least these auto walas want me, unlike all the past girls I have liked in my life...
If you're aboard one of these autos going to the "Tation", boy, are you in for a ride. The ability to drive more rashly than a drunk man while actually being sober is baffling. At first, you fear for your life. But once you're habituated to it, you learn to enjoy the thrill. Heck, if your corporate slave life has left you feeling dead inside, these auto rides will surely make you feel alive again.

This place is my prison. It's just that my shackles are invisible. Everyday I am forced to come back here to give away my youth to work. How are the rest of you coping? Does it not get frustrating at some point? Doesn't it feel like everyday is on repeat? I get it, we've to do it for money. But still..

Maybe I really should quit my job. But preparing for interviews on the weekends is agony. I'm stuck in this corporate hell.

When I look down at the people from my office's glass window, they seem so miserable. Moving like ants in a line, desperate to return home to their families.

The beautiful sunsets and skies that you can view from here almost feels like a poetic joke made by the universe. For it's a stark contrast to the hell that is my work place. Still, it soothes me a little. I've attached a few photos of the sceneries for reference.
I've seen many seasons come and go here, be it rain, the scorching summer or the flimsy winter. The only thing that hasn't changed during this time is myself. I am still miserable.

Maybe computer engineering was a mistake. I don't like it particularly in the first place. Everyone these days is a Software Engineer. Hearing that title makes me cringe inside, like the bad aftertaste of a medicine. It's so boring that everyone around is a software engineer. Why don't I get to meet people who say "I am a psychologist" or "I am a writer" or something cool like that?

Is a so called stable job that important? Stability, but at what cost? Your whole mental health? How does it feel to have become a human whose primal fear is not heights, not a wild animal, not death, but something as lame as a Monday?

Even as I say this, I know that I need to go back to this place. I need to earn. Money is happiness, after all. But we are working everyday for someone else's dream; someone we don't even know, a system who doesn't even know or care about your existence.

Just like Sisyphus, I keep doing this meaningless task, apparently forever.

Apart from all that, the infrastructure and maintenance here is good 😊 The restrooms are hygienic as well.

P.S. I thought this review was really funny but sadly I think it got taken down :( Hence, posting this again.

This is by far the WORST and most pathetic society I have ever come across! 🤦🏻‍♂️
There are so many problems in this building, yet the broker conveniently hides all the issues and assures you that everything is fine just to get you to rent a flat. Once you move in and the problems start surfacing, you are left to deal with everything on your own. There is absolutely no one willing to listen or help!

Here are some of the major problems with this society:
👉🏻 Poor cleanliness and hygiene: The society is not cleaned properly. There is garbage and dirt everywhere.

👉🏻 A serious stray dog menace: Having pet dogs is perfectly fine, but this society is infested with stray dogs. They can attack you at any time. I have personally been attacked twice while jogging in the morning! And guess what? There is nobody to listen to your complaints or take any action. Every night, 50–60 dogs bark and fight continuously, making it almost impossible to sleep peacefully. There is no one to control the situation.

👉🏻 Absolutely NO mobile network: No mobile network from any telecom company works properly anywhere in the society. Without a Wi-Fi connection, your mobile phone is practically useless here. If you need to make a call, you have to go to the balcony and try your luck. If someone calls you, the call simply won't connect. You can only communicate if they contact you through WhatsApp calls or messages over Wi-Fi.

👉🏻 An unacceptable and ongoing water supply crisis: I rented a flat here in March, and by April 20, the water supply to the washrooms had completely stopped. Water was available only in the kitchen. Initially, I thought it would be a temporary issue, so I shifted to a hotel. I spent seven days there, but when the water supply still hadn't resumed, I was forced to return to the flat.
For three continuous months, not a single drop of water came into the washrooms! Imagine having to fill buckets in the kitchen and carry them to the washrooms just to manage basic daily needs. 🤦🏻‍♂️
The water supply resumed around June 23–24, but that didn't last either. From June 23–24 until today, October 28, water has been available for barely 24–25 days in total! They supply water to the washrooms for one day and then shut it off for the next four or five days. This ridiculous cycle continues even today.

👉🏻 Security concerns and an unresponsive management: Security in this society seems to have been left entirely to fate. The management simply refuses to listen to residents' complaints. It feels as though nobody is willing to take responsibility or address even the most basic problems.

MY ADVICE TO ANYONE CONSIDERING BUYING OR RENTING A FLAT HERE: Please think twice before making a decision. If you are prepared to put up with all these problems, you are welcome to move in. Otherwise, stay as far away from this society as possible!

A home should provide peace, safety, and basic necessities-not constant stress, sleepless nights, water shortages, and helplessness.

BEWARE! Do your own research and thoroughly check everything before committing to a flat here. 🙏🏻

The only 4 or 5-star reviews you see here are from people who just saw the sample flat or interacted with the sales team. Some are probably old reviews too.
